learning: Iteration 6 showed the 0.016 footprint hurts the oval (finish 1.0 to 0.55) without fixing the slalom. Iteration 5 showed narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 raised s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42 with the oval still at 20 of 20. Whether 0.09 keeps the oval stable is the open question, and the race answers it.
notes: Adopts the Builder's proposal: sensor_size reverted to 0.012, wheel_track 0.09 m, and the row widened to x=±0.07 at y=0.08. The controller is iteration 5's best set, held fixed. Oscillation and oval finish rate are watched for the narrower-track risk.
rationale: Iteration 6 is the key evidence. Raising sensor_size to 0.016 cut the oval finish rate from 1.0 to 0.55 and left the slalom at one line loss per run, so the larger footprint is rejected. Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10, sensor 0.012, row at y=0.08 with x=±0.06) remains the best design at 386.35: oval 20 of 20 finishes, s-bend progress 0.42. The s-bend still leaves the track at max_error 0.0624 with 0.1 line losses, which is turn-rate limited, so I adopt the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m. Iteration 5 showed the oval tolerates a narrower track, so 0.09 is a reasonable step, though it is the main risk. The slalom still loses the line once per run with x=±0.06, so the Builder's row widening to x=±0.07 at y=0.08 with sensor_size 0.012 gives the outer sensors more reach. Controller values are held at iteration 5 (kp 5.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.8, weights -1.5/-0.75/0/0.75/1.5, base_speed 1.6, last_direction). Kd stays at 0.8 to damp the extra yaw from the narrower track. Two geometry variables change (track and row width), which I accept with four iterations left. Expected: s-bend max_error at or below 0.061 m, s-bend progress at or above 0.42, slalom line losses below 1.0, oval finish rate at or above 0.85. If the oval finish rate falls below 0.85 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, revert wheel_track to 0.10 first.
